key_insight: THz time-domain spectroscopy can non-destructively fingerprint specific grain-boundary defects in organic halide perovskite films and quantify them via defect-specific absorption strength.
engineering_relevance: This enables a closed-loop defect screening and passivation workflow for improving perovskite solar-cell efficiency and reliability.
method: Measure 0.3–3.0 THz spectra of thin-film perovskites at room temperature.
Identify intrinsic phonon peaks and grain-boundary-localized defect vibrations by composition.
Use oscillator-strength analysis to quantify defect concentration and guide passivation.
evidence_signal: Across MAPbI3, MAPbBr3, FAPbI3, and CsPbI3 films, the 1.58 THz MAPbI3 absorption scales linearly with XPS-quantified CH3NH2 defect concentration.
watch_item: The approach depends on a curated THz fingerprint library and may need composition-specific calibration before it can be used broadly in manufacturing.
paper_title: Terahertz Time-Domain Spectroscopy as a Universal Defect Fingerprinting Tool for Organic Halide Perovskite Solar Cells
